pull_request.title: Share bounded sparse memory image fixture loading
pull_request.body:
Jobs currently expands sparse frozen memory images locally before checking that retired ledgers are refused without writes. Add `testing::memory_from_sparse_hex(pages, runs, maximum_pages)` so Memory owns the fixture backing mechanics. Jobs keeps image provenance, its JSON schema, payload admission and both fresh/recovery refusal assertions.

The helper creates fresh zero-filled VectorMemory only, under an explicit page ceiling. It validates address bounds and ASCII hexadecimal runs before backing allocation, preserves gaps/trailing zeros and applies overlaps in input order. `SparseMemoryImageError` carries typed page/run/growth refusals. It never opens a runtime, recovers allocation authority, converts formats or accepts existing backing. The API is behind `test-support`; dependencies, package versions and runtime/storage contracts are unchanged. Compatible pending notes are 0.46.1 against released 0.46.0; the owner's pending 0.47 work remains separate.

Validation on Linux x86_64:
- Five focused producer tests pass on actual Rust 1.91: exact bytes/gaps/page boundaries/overlaps, page ceilings, malformed/non-ASCII hex, out-of-bounds runs, empty images and substrate growth refusal.
- Strict library/test Clippy, Rust 1.91 Wasm with test-support, warning-denied Rust 1.91 rustdoc, formatting and changed-document link checks pass. The link check used Jobs' reviewed Shared 0.16 checker; no tooling payload was copied into Memory.
- An isolated Jobs caller passes 25 consumer tests, 19 composition tests and one independent comparison reproducing both complete frozen backings byte for byte with the previous expansion. The caller's Wasm floor and strict Clippy also pass. All package names/versions remain selected; only Memory's source/checksum lock row is substituted for qualification.

Jobs' active registry dependency and local expansion remain until reviewed publication; the adoption patch is prepared separately. This contribution is independent of #120's fixture-runtime bootstrap. No full release suite, native macOS, live PocketIC, reset, release or publication ran. No sibling checkout was modified.

Reviewed this contribution and integrated its exact sparse-image source into Memory's working tree on released 0.47.0 (`b179ab9514b549f4ede75afd3757db264d3ce412`). The module exports coexist with the delivered fixture-runtime API. Pending compatible notes are now 0.47.1; no package version or dependency selection was changed by this integration. The incoming owner-selected Host 0.25.1 lockfile update is preserved.

Focused combined-tree checks pass: all 15 fixture tests on Rust 1.99, the five sparse-image tests on actual Rust 1.91, strict library/test/repo-tool Clippy, Rust 1.91 Wasm compilation with test-support, all 56 release-helper tests, formatting and diff checks. The helper remains fixture-only; ordinary production builds exclude its module. Stored bytes, allocation authority and production APIs are unchanged.

Keep this PR open until owner delivery and CI acceptance of the combined source. Jobs' registry adoption and removal of its local loader remain consumer work after publication; this integration does not claim those changes. No PR merge, commit, release, installed qualification or sibling-checkout edit was performed.

Closing as already integrated through the direct release flow, rather than merging this older 0.46-based branch. The complete `sparse_image.rs` at PR head `1b80f9c55129a5fb55ffc7839943f39368627089` is byte-identical to its delivery in `fb716877c730377abed6eb6b301bb3fbee31cabe`, released as Memory 0.48.0, and current public main `f2abbdac950379677259ac9311ce5cb9984b7aa0` (0.48.1). The test-support export, package README and 0.48 root/detail notes are present. Five focused sparse-image tests pass again with Rust 1.99, locked/offline. All ten PR hosted checks already passed. No merge, branch deletion or release is needed; downstream consumers still qualify their own published adoption.

issue.body:
## Implemented and qualified on main

`apps/job-consumer/src/queue/tests.rs::prior_memory_ledgers_are_refused_without_writes_or_reset` imports Memory `testing::memory_from_sparse_hex`, calls it with a three-page ceiling and no longer owns the expansion loop. Both frozen images, producer assertions, outer/payload refusal and zero-write/unchanged-backing checks remain. Locked Memory is 0.48.2.

Reviewed against delivered Jobs **0.17.2**, [`177a4dd4aa9a22492830839fec0ea6e42c5d234c`](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-jobs/commit/177a4dd4aa9a22492830839fec0ea6e42c5d234c), with reviewed Shared snapshot `6eb8c41785c5156aef62f082702bd54e8ce04606` (0.24.0 annotation). The maintainer checkout's unrelated dirty dependency refresh is excluded.

The matching [CI run](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-jobs/actions/runs/39139517213) now passes the complete Linux, Apple Silicon and Intel macOS native matrix on that exact delivered source. The owned caller/fixture checks remain present as described above. This completes this adoption outcome; native CI does not establish live PocketIC recovery. No workflow dispatch/rerun, package release or publication was performed by this reconciliation.

<details>
<summary>Historical preparation and earlier acceptance observations</summary>

Memory PR https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/pull/121 adds the fixture-only `testing::memory_from_sparse_hex(pages, runs, maximum_pages)` helper. Qualified producer source: `1b80f9c55129a5fb55ffc7839943f39368627089`, based on published Memory 0.46.0 `578a25a15575c1e2c54439c41fc1866a847e006a`.

Jobs' incoming pending 0.15 tree on `cc9587c` still expands sparse frozen backings inside `apps/job-consumer/src/queue/tests.rs::prior_memory_ledgers_are_refused_without_writes_or_reset`. Keep that active implementation until the reviewed helper is published; there is no active Git/path dependency or copied upstream fallback.

Prepared adoption patch: `target/qualification/entry-image-cleanup/memory-adoption.patch`. It removes the local page-growth/hex/write loop, imports only fresh fixture backing under a three-page ceiling, and starts IO observation after import. Jobs retains both exact frozen image files, producer labels, its schema/payload refusal, allocation opening and zero-write/unchanged-page/unchanged-backing assertions for both fresh and recovery entrypoints.

Acceptance:
- Select the reviewed published Memory release containing the helper and apply the prepared patch; keep the published Jobs package dependency boundary unchanged.
- Re-run the affected consumer checks on actual Rust 1.91 and qualify the supported hosts; maintain exact frozen bytes and existing refusal ordering. No runtime reset, conversion or old-format decoder is introduced.
- Retire the local expansion loop completely once registry adoption is qualified.

Evidence: `target/qualification/entry-image-cleanup/`. The isolated caller at `/tmp/jobs-entry-image-cleanup.vwYbY7/consumer` passes 25 consumer tests, 19 composition tests and an independent reference comparison reproducing both complete frozen backings byte for byte. Its Rust 1.91 Wasm check and strict Clippy pass. Only Memory's source/checksum row differs in the candidate lockfile; package names/versions are unchanged. Producer qualification includes five Rust 1.91 tests, strict library/test Clippy, Rust 1.91 Wasm, warning-denied rustdoc, formatting and documentation links. Linux evidence does not establish native macOS or live IC recovery; full CI/live/release/publication were not run.


</details>

 # Changelog
 
+## [0.46.1]
+
+- Add bounded sparse hexadecimal image loading under `test-support` for fresh
+  fixture backing. Runtime authority, stored formats and production APIs are unchanged.
+
+[Detailed notes](docs/changelog/0.46.md)
+
 ## [0.46.0] - 2026-10-17
 
 - **Breaking ownership API:** allocation handles are non-cloneable leases.

@@ -365,6 +365,12 @@ work budgets and restored-state/lifecycle validation; fresh empty bytes must
 never substitute for a required retained journal. Bootstrap may update ledger
 metadata before a later Cell refusal, and backing IO can still panic.
 
+For frozen sparse backing fixtures, `testing::memory_from_sparse_hex` expands
+ordered `(offset, hex)` runs into fresh zero-filled VectorMemory with an explicit
+page ceiling. It checks bounds and hex before backing allocation and reports
+typed failures. Callers retain provenance, schema and payload validation. This
+helper does not open a runtime, recover authority or convert retained formats.
+
 - [Operations and diagnostics](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/blob/main/docs/operations.md)
   explains memory attribution, bucket configuration, and runtime reports.
 - [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md)

@@ -1,5 +1,18 @@
 # 0.46 release notes
 
+## [0.46.1]
+
+`testing::memory_from_sparse_hex` expands ordered offset/hex runs into fresh
+zero-filled VectorMemory under an explicit caller-selected page ceiling. It
+checks address bounds and ASCII hex before backing allocation, retaining gaps,
+trailing zeros and ordered overlaps. Typed failures identify page limits,
+offending runs and substrate growth refusal.
+
+This is fixture import only. Callers keep provenance, schema/JSON and payload
+admission; no runtime is opened and no authority or stored-format conversion is
+performed. Existing backing is never an input. The helper is behind
+`test-support`, without new dependencies or changed runtime/storage contracts.
+
 ## [0.46.0] - 2026-10-17
 
 [#118 — Enforce exclusive allocation leases and narrow substrate exports](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/issues/118)
